title: Eventual vanishing of affine higher direct image sections
statement: Let I be a nonempty directed preorder and X_i an inverse system over a scheme S [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transitions and qcqs structure maps, with limit X whose structure map is qcqs. Let F_i be compatible abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], with unital and composable transition maps f_ji^* F_i to F_j [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Set F = colim_i f_i^* F_i. Fix p >= 0. Let K be a presentation of the directed diagram R^p g_i,* F_i [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and eta its canonical comparison cocone into R^p g_* F, using [def-sbc-abelian-higher-direct-image-map]. For every affine etale object $V\to S$ and every $z\in K_i(V)$ with $\eta_i(V)(z)=0$, there exist $j\in I$ and $f:i\to j$ such that $K(f)(V)(z)=0$. Here $K_i(V)$ denotes sections on V of the sheaf in the given presentation.

source.place: Tag 09Z1, proof on qcqs etale objects; Tag 03Q8

proof.text: By the higher direct image presheaf theorem, locally lift a stage sheaf section to restricted cohomology. Naturality of the derived adjunction comparison identifies the maps with the canonical cohomology comparisons specified by hK and hη. Since the limit sheaf section is zero, refine the neighborhood to make the limit cohomology representative zero. Refine further by affine etale objects.

On each affine member U, base change of the scheme diagram and cone preserves the limit and affine transitions. The maps to affine U are qcqs, hence the stages and limit are qcqs schemes. Exact inverse image preserves the colimit and degree-zero complexes. Apply complex cohomology continuity with lower bound zero. Its injectivity and the filtered-colimit equality criterion imply that the restricted cohomology representative vanishes at a later stage.

The affine V is quasi-compact, so finitely many of these etale neighborhoods cover it. Choose a common later stage for their finitely many indices and compose transitions. There the original section is zero on the cover by naturality of the presheaf comparison, hence zero by separatedness of the higher direct image sheaf.
